ei.title: Literacy Gaps in New Food Alternatives
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: When we were investigating why Americans valued meat so much, we found widespread confusion among consumers about which foods are healthy and sustainable. As part of the project, we asked consumers to sort different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped. Participants ended up dividing foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies hinder the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health benefits.

questions.passage: When we were investigating why Americans valued meat so much, we found ①<u>widespread</u> confusion among consumers about which foods are ②<u>healthily</u> and sustainable. As part of the project, we asked consumers to sort different foods in any way they thought they should be ③<u>grouped</u>. Participants ended up ④<u>dividing</u> foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies hinder the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: healthily → healthy. be동사 보어 = 형용사
det.analysis:
❌ ① widespread — 'widespread confusion'에서 명사 수식 형용사. 적절
✅ ② healthily — 원문은 healthy. 'which foods are healthy'에서 be동사 보어로 형용사 필요. healthily(부사)는 보어 불가 ←정답
❌ ③ grouped — 'they should be grouped'에서 수동태(be + p.p.) 구조. 적절
❌ ④ dividing — 'ended up dividing'에서 end up + -ing. 적절
det.tip: foods are healthy — be동사 + 형용사(보어). 부사 healthily는 동사를 수식하는 역할

questions.passage: When we were investigating why Americans ①<u>valued</u> meat so much, we found widespread confusion among consumers about which foods are healthy and sustainable. As part of the project, we asked consumers to ②<u>sort</u> different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped. Participants ended up dividing foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be ③<u>similarly</u> to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies hinder the successful implementation of products that ④<u>could</u> have environmental and health benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: similar → similarly 오류. be동사 보어 = 형용사
det.analysis:
❌ ① valued — 'why Americans valued meat'에서 과거 시제 동사. 적절
❌ ② sort — 'asked consumers to sort'에서 to부정사 원형. 적절
✅ ③ similarly — 원문은 similar. 'will likely be similar to'에서 be동사 보어로 형용사 필요. similarly(부사)는 보어 역할 불가 ←정답
❌ ④ could — 'products that could have'에서 가능성의 조동사. 적절
det.tip: be similar to — be동사 + 형용사(보어) + 전치사

However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. ③<u>Interestingly</u>, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies hinder the successful implementation of products ④<u>what</u> could have environmental and health benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: what → that. 선행사 products 있으므로 관계대명사 that 필요
det.analysis:
❌ ① which — 'about which foods are'에서 전치사+관계대명사 구조. 적절
❌ ② ended up — 'Participants ended up dividing'에서 과거 시제. 적절
❌ ③ Interestingly — 문장 부사. 적절
✅ ④ what — 원문은 that. 'products that could have'에서 선행사 products를 수식하는 관계대명사 that 필요. what은 선행사 포함 관계대명사로 선행사 products와 중복 ←정답
det.tip: products that could have — 선행사(products) + 관계대명사(that). what = the thing which

questions.passage: When we were ①<u>investigating</u> why Americans valued meat so much, we found widespread confusion among consumers about which foods are healthy and sustainable. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies ③<u>enhance</u> the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health ④<u>benefits</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 기술 문해력 격차가 시행을 '방해한다'는 맥락. enhance(향상시키다)는 hinder(방해하다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① investigating — 원문 일치. '육류를 좋아하는 이유를 조사하는 중'에 적절
❌ ② dividing — 원문 일치. '음식을 그룹으로 나누었다'에 적절
✅ ③ enhance — 원문은 hinder(방해하다). enhance(향상시키다)로 바꾸면 '격차가 시행을 향상시킨다'가 되어 모순 ←정답
❌ ④ benefits — 원문 일치. '환경적·건강적 혜택'에 적절
det.tip: gaps hinder the successful implementation — 격차가 시행을 방해(hinder)한다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 배양육 반응이 유전자 변형 식품 반응과 '유사할' 것이라는 맥락. contrary(반대의)는 similar(유사한)의 반의어로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① valued — 원문 일치. '미국인들이 고기를 좋아하는(valued) 이유'에 적절
❌ ② typical — 원문 일치. '어떤 전형적인(typical) 식품군에도 속하지 않는다'에 적절
✅ ③ contrary — 원문은 similar. 'will likely be similar to'에서 similar를 contrary로 바꾸면 '반대일 것'이 되어 유사성 맥락과 모순 ←정답
❌ ④ emerging — 원문 일치. '신흥(emerging) 기술'에 적절
det.tip: will likely be similar to — 유사할 가능성이 높다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 식품이 건강하고 지속 가능한지에 대해 소비자들 사이에서 널리 퍼진 혼란을 발견했다
det.analysis:
❌ ① negative reactions: '부정적 반응'은 유전자 변형 식품 맥락이지 '발견한' 대상으로 부적합
✅ ② widespread confusion: 원문 일치. '소비자들 사이에 널리 퍼진 혼란' ←정답
❌ ③ meat alternatives: '고기 대안'은 분류 대상이지 '발견한 것' 자체가 아님
❌ ④ successful implementation: '성공적 시행'은 방해당하는 대상이지 '발견한' 대상 아님
det.tip: we found widespread confusion — 이후 분류 실패, 배양육 불신이 혼란의 구체적 사례

det.analysis:
❌ ① plant-based milks: '식물 기반 우유'는 분류 불능 맥락이지 부정적 반응 비교 대상 아님
❌ ② lab-grown meats: '배양육'은 반응의 주체이지 비교 대상이 아님
❌ ③ meat alternatives: '고기 대안'은 분류 불능 맥락이지 시장 출시 시 부정적 반응 대상 아님
✅ ④ genetically modified foods: 원문 일치. 유전자 변형 식품에 대한 부정적 반응 ←정답

questions.passage: When we were investigating why Americans valued meat so much, we found widespread confusion among consumers about which foods are healthy and sustainable. As part of the project, we asked consumers to sort different foods in any way <u>they</u> thought they should be grouped. Participants ended up dividing foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies hinder the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health benefits.
questions.stem: 윗글에서 밑줄 친 they(5번째 문장: Interestingly, they didn't consider them ...)가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: they = most consumers. 4번째 문장의 주어 most consumers를 받는 대명사
det.analysis:
✅ ① 4번째 문장 'most consumers didn't know how to sort'의 주어 most consumers를 5번째 문장 they가 받음 ←정답
❌ ② 식물 기반 우유는 분류 대상(목적어)이지 분류 주체(주어)가 아님
❌ ③ 고기 대안 식품도 분류 대상이지 주체가 아님
❌ ④ 연구 참여자들(participants)은 3번째 문장 주어이고 4번째부터 most consumers로 전환
det.tip: most consumers(4문장) → they(5문장)
